events.title: The Gregorian calendar begins
events.shortBlurb: By decree of Pope Gregory XIII the calendar leapt from 4 October straight to 15 October to correct the drift of the seasons…
body: The Julian calendar, in use since 45 BC, ran some eleven minutes too long in each year; over fifteen centuries the error had carried the spring equinox, by which Easter is reckoned, from 21 March, where the Council of Nicaea had fixed it in 325, back toward 11 March. The Council of Trent had left the correction to the Holy See.

Acting on the plan of the Calabrian astronomer Aloysius Lilius, refined and defended by the Jesuit mathematician Christopher Clavius, Pope Gregory XIII decreed the reform in the bull Inter gravissimas, dated 24 February 1582. Ten days were cut from that year: Thursday 4 October was followed at once by Friday 15 October. Henceforth century years would be leap years only when divisible by four hundred.

Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Poland adopted the new reckoning at once; Protestant and Orthodox lands followed only over the next three centuries. Teresa of Ávila died at Alba de Tormes on the very night of the change, so that the day after her death was reckoned 15 October, the day her feast is still kept.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “The Reform of the Calendar”
